words.gloss: in the house of the trusting

literal: Than the dead different they are not surely, in the house of those who trusted evil having done those who behave.
translation: Those who behave by doing evil in the house of those who trusted them are surely no different from the dead.
modern: தங்களை நம்பியவரின் வீட்டில் தீமை செய்து நடப்பவர்கள், நிச்சயமாக இறந்தவர்களை விட வேறுபட்டவர்கள் அல்லர்.
explanation: This couplet strongly condemns betraying a friend's trust by violating the sanctity of their home. The word 'தெளிந்தார்' refers to those who have placed clear trust in the offender, while 'இல்' means house, specifically pointing to the household or wife in the context of this chapter. By committing 'தீமை' (evil) in such a trusting home, the betrayer loses all moral standing. The poet declares that such people are 'விளிந்தாரின் வேறல்லர்'—no different from the dead—because a life lived with such deceit is devoid of true vitality or virtue.
